# hcloudplus_project_token (Resource)

A project-scoped API token for use against the public Hetzner Cloud API. The `secret` output is returned once at creation time; store it in Pulumi/Terraform state (encrypted) and pass it to hcloud-go / terraform-provider-hcloud as needed. Tokens are immutable: any change to `description` or `readonly` forces replacement.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hcloudplus_project" "example" {
  name = "infra-prod"
}

# Read-write token for use with the upstream hcloud provider.
resource "hcloudplus_project_token" "rw" {
  project_id  = hcloudplus_project.example.id
  description = "pulumi-rw"
  readonly    = false
}

# Hand the secret to the upstream hcloud provider.
provider "hcloud" {
  alias = "infra_prod"
  token = hcloudplus_project_token.rw.secret
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) Human-readable description of the token (shown in the Hetzner console).
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project this token belongs to, as a string (e.g. `hcloudplus_project.x.id`).

### Optional

- `readonly` (Boolean) Whether the token has read-only scope. Defaults to false (read-write).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Numeric token ID as a string.
- `prefix` (String) First-half prefix of the token, used to identify it in audit logs.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The full 64-character bearer token. Only populated on create — Hetzner does not return it on subsequent reads.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import format: <project_id>:<token_id>
# Note: the `secret` attribute is UNKNOWN after import — Hetzner does not
# return it on subsequent reads. Any downstream provider that consumes the
# secret will need a fresh token created via terraform.
terraform import hcloudplus_project_token.rw 14138093:177763691
```
